response: ["Surgical excision with histologically negative margins is the recommended and first-line treatment for primary cutaneous melanoma of any thickness, as well as for melanoma in situ.","Surgical margins for melanoma should be based on tumor thickness.","Sentinel lymph node biopsy, when indicated, should be performed before wide excision of the primary tumor.","Sentinel lymph node biopsy should be performed in the same operative setting as wide excision whenever possible.","When melanoma is suspected, the whole lesion should be completely excised with a narrow (1-3 mm) margin to perform histological diagnosis.","Incisional biopsies can be performed on large lesions such as lesions on the face (e.g., lentigo maligna), acral lesions, and on the genitalia.","The 7-point score is driven by the presence of a blue‑whitish veil, which contributes 2 points.","The 7-point score is also driven by the presence of diffuse irregular pigmentation, which contributes 1 point.","A blue‑whitish veil is defined as confluent blue pigment with an overlying white haze.","Diffuse irregular pigmentation is defined as asymmetric blotches of pigment.","The other criteria (pigment network, vascular structures, streaks, dots and globules, regression structures) were scored as absent or typical and contributed 0 points.","The criteria driving the 7-point score are major and minor criteria respectively, each scoring maximally under their respective categories."]
